Dan (AE): looping sec folks — prospect's security reviewer (Eve) asked for specifics on at-rest encryption, BYOK/HSM options, and key rotation for a Dedicated deployment. Ticket #4821.
Alice (SE): short answer: AES-256-GCM at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, envelope encryption with data keys encrypted by a KEK (customer-managed CMK supported). For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / Google KMS) and BYOK via HSM-backed import or key-wrap flows. Keys are never stored in plaintext on our boxes. :lock:
Eve (Customer Sec): can you confirm the attestation level for the HSM (FIPS level) and whether keys ever leave our HSM during inference? Also want rotation cadence guidance.
Claire (Security): we support HSM-backed workflows. Customers can use AWS CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2 validated modules) or bring their own HSM for on-prem/private installs. For BYOK we accept wrapped keys — we never have access to the unwrapped private key material.
Ben (Infra): example config we give customers for Private deployment (YAML snippet):
```
kms:
  provider: aws
  mode: byok
  key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
  wrap: true  # use customer wrapping key
  rotation_policy: customer_managed
```
Alice (SE): rotation guidance: recommend customer rotate CMKs per their policy (common: 90 days). Redwood does not silently rewrap customer-managed CMKs; we can schedule rewrap operations with the customer if they want automated rollover. For service-managed keys (hosted API) we rotate per infra policy and log events.
Eve (Customer Sec): need an explicit statement for vendor risk review: "Do keys ever leave our control?" and HSM attestation docs (certs).
Claire (Security): approved wording we can use for RFPs: "Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM; when BYOK is configured, keys are imported or wrapped by the customer and Redwood stores only encrypted key material. Redwood does not have the capability to export unwrapped customer key material from customer-managed HSMs. We provide HSM attestation and CloudHSM reports on request under NDA."
Dan (AE): perfect — can you attach the CAIQ/SIG pack and the HSM attestation link we hand to enterprise?
Claire (Security): uploading: CAIQ v3 (completed), SIG Lite answers, SOC2 summary, and sample CloudHSM attestation redaction pack. Link: https://redwood.example/ent/sec-deliverables/4821 (internal). I'll PM legal for the non-disclosure cadence on full certs.
Ben (Infra): note on runtime: inference memory may hold encrypted keys in secure memory; we use envelope encryption so the long-term KEK stays in HSM and only short-lived DEKs are used in-process, rewrapped per request. No plaintext KEKs on disk.
Eve (Customer Sec): ok — last Q: do you support client-side proof-of-possession or HSM pin challenge for operations?
Alice (SE): we support key-wrapping and attestation workflows; for customer on-prem HSMs you can require HSM PINs / auth as part of your orchestration. For AWS KMS, access is governed by IAM policies and key grants; we can integrate with your access controls.
Dan (AE): I'll send this pack to the prospect. Claire/Alice — can you produce a single-paragraph vendor-safe answer and a one-page checkbox list for the RFP?
Claire (Security): yes — I'll drop the approved one-paragraph and a checklist in this thread in ~30m. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: docs uploaded to secure bucket: s3://redwood-sec/4821/caqi-sig.zip
Alice (SE): thanks everyone — will follow up if the customer asks for a live demo of the BYOK import flow during the POC.
Eve (Customer Sec): thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
